summary: Kenji Kinugawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at Kyoto University (~1971–1980) under Seizan Yanagida. His students include Eric M. Greene.
Kenji Matsuo is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1984) and held a post at Yamagata University (~1987–2020).
Kenji Shimada (1917–2000) was a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1938–1941) and served as a researcher there from around 1949 to 1981.

Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Diwakar Acharya, Yuko Yokochi, and Peter C. Bisschop at Leiden University. He held posts at Kyoto University (attested 2018) and the University of Naples Federico II (2019–2021).
Kenji Watanabe is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held an assistant post at Taisho University in 1978 and studied under Jozef Deleu from around 1982 to 1985.

Kenjiu Kasawara (1851–1883) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879, with teachers including Friedrich Max Müller (1879–1882) and Arthur Anthony Macdonell.

Kenjuro Yanagida (1893–1983) was a philosopher who studied at Yokohama National University (~1913–1916) and under Kitarō Nishida (~1922–1925). He held an academic post at Hirosaki University (~1949–1950).
Kenkai Naganuma (1883–1980) specialized in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He served as professor emeritus at Kyushu University (~1946–1980) and held a post at Kurume University (~1950–1958).
Kennard Lipman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who completed doctoral work under Herbert V. Günther. He has served as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.

Kenneth Adrian Raine Kennedy (1930–2014) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1954–1962) and held a long-term post at Cornell University (~1964–2005).
Kenneth Doo Young Lee works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed doctoral studies under Ryuichi Abe at Columbia University and held a post at Stetson University (attested 2007).

Kenneth G. Zysk is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who earned an M.A. from UC Santa Barbara and a Ph.D. from Australian National University. His academic posts include Eastern Michigan University and the University of Copenhagen.

Kenneth J. Guest is a religious studies and sinology scholar who studied at Peking University, Columbia, Union Theological Seminary, and CUNY. He has held academic posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under W. D. C. Wagiswara. From around 1921 to 1935, he served at the Pacific School of Religion and the University of California.

Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who taught at the University at Buffalo. He chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research and the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism (1996–1999).

Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Stanford, IBS, the University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley. He served on the faculty at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and Musashino University.
Kenneth R. Valpey is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara. He has held a post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Kenneth Roy Norman (1925–2020) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Downing College, Cambridge. He served as a lecturer and reader at the University of Cambridge and edited the Journal of the Pali Text Society (1981–1994).

Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He held faculty posts at Aichi Gakuin University (2000–2010), the University of Tokyo (from 2010), and Rissho University (2025).
Kenryu Tsuji (1919–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued his education at Ryukoku University (1938) and the University of Toronto.
